$comment: Rule catalog — bankroll and staking. Standards 11 and 12. This file carries four of the pack's prohibitions, all of them variations on one behaviour: letting a loss decide the next stake.

rules.title: The bankroll is declared
rules.description: A ring-fenced bankroll is declared, and every decision records the bankroll it was sized against.
rules.rationale: Every cap in this pack is a fraction of the bankroll. Without a declared figure the caps are fractions of nothing, and 'a big bet' and 'a small bet' have no meaning that can be checked.
rules.remediation: Declare the bankroll and record it on each decision.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance that a bankroll is declared and recorded. That the declared figure is money genuinely set aside for wagering is outside what a record can show.

rules.title: A unit is defined as a fraction of bankroll
rules.description: The betting policy defines one unit as a fraction of bankroll, and the Kelly multiplier used for sizing.
rules.rationale: A unit lets stakes be discussed and compared without reference to a bankroll figure, and it keeps sizing proportional as the bankroll moves.
rules.remediation: Set unitPercent and kellyMultiplier in betting-policy.yml.
rules.$assuranceNote: Full assurance that both are defined and well-formed.

rules.title: Stakes follow the declared sizing rule
rules.description: No stake exceeds the recommended stake produced by the declared sizing rule, or the single-bet cap.
rules.rationale: A sizing rule that is followed when convenient is not a sizing rule. The cap exists because Kelly optimises growth under a correct probability estimate, and the estimate is exactly the thing that might be wrong.
rules.remediation: Reduce the stake to the recommended amount, or record the decision as a PASS.

rules.title: Losses are never chased
rules.description: No wager is placed, and no stake is increased, in order to recover a previous loss. Each decision is made on its own edge, price, and exposure, as though the ledger before it were empty.
rules.rationale: Chasing is what turns a bad night into a bad year. The mechanism is that a loss creates an urgency the next wager did not earn, and the wager gets placed because money is owed to the past rather than because a price is wrong in the present.
rules.remediation: Evaluate the next decision on its own merits. If it does not clear the threshold on its own, it is a PASS regardless of what came before.
rules.$assuranceNote: NOT MECHANICALLY EVALUATED. Chasing is defined by motive, and motive is not in the record: a wager placed to recover a loss is indistinguishable from the same wager placed on its merits. The mechanical shadow of this rule is bankroll.no-loss-driven-sizing, which detects the sizing pattern chasing usually produces. This rule reports not-evaluated unless a human attests to it, and MUST NOT be reported as satisfied because nothing was found.

rules.title: No Martingale-style loss recovery
rules.description: No staking scheme increases the stake after a loss with the intent of recovering it, whether by doubling or by any other progression.
rules.rationale: Martingale converts a series of small losses into one catastrophic one, and it feels safe right up until it is not. Each step is individually survivable; the sequence is bounded only by the bankroll, and the bankroll always runs out before the losing streak does.
rules.remediation: Size every wager from its own edge and the declared rule. Delete the progression.
rules.$assuranceNote: Detects repeated stake increases following losses that the records' own sizing arithmetic does not support. A single escalation reports as a warning; two or more consecutive escalations report as this violation. An escalation the bettor's own Kelly maths justifies does NOT fire, because it is indistinguishable from discipline — so this check can be evaded by a progression that stays inside the recommended stake.

rules.title: Bet size never increases because previous bets lost
rules.description: The size of a wager is a function of its own edge, price, and the declared sizing rule. Prior results are not an input to it.
rules.rationale: Past results carry no information about the next wager's edge, so letting them move the stake adds variance without adding expectation. It is the same error as the gambler's fallacy, expressed in money rather than in probability.
rules.remediation: Recompute the stake from this wager's own edge and the sizing rule.
rules.$assuranceNote: Detects a stake that grew after a loss AND exceeds the record's own recommended stake. A loss-driven increase that stays within the recommended stake is not distinguishable from ordinary sizing and is not reported.

rules.title: Risk is never increased because an outcome is 'due'
rules.description: No stake is raised on the grounds that a person, team, or outcome is overdue, owed a result, or bound to turn.
rules.rationale: Nothing is ever due. This is the gambler's fallacy applied to sizing rather than to probability, and it is more dangerous there: an unchanged probability estimate hides the error while the stake carries it.
rules.remediation: Size from the edge. If the belief that something is due is real, it belongs in the probability estimate with a causal justification, where it can be examined.
rules.$assuranceNote: NOT MECHANICALLY EVALUATED. The reasoning behind a stake is not in the record. The prose scan for the phrase 'due for' is a courtesy that catches the careless case only, and this rule reports not-evaluated unless a human attests to it.
